archive.title: Competitive Circuit Proposal
archive.summary: A product-strategy draft with paid-only progression and unsupported legal claims requiring replacement or major rewrite.
archive.provenance: Archived PDF reviewed during the Archive Diagnostic.
archive.body:
## Why it remains in the archive

This proposal records an important product experiment and the tensions it revealed. It should be preserved as strategy history, not silently discarded.

## Why it must not guide implementation

K-XP from paid events is required for major qualification, paid participation becomes a proxy for legitimacy, and the document calls the structure legally clean without qualified review. Those elements contradict the player-first direction.

archive.title: Para Poker
archive.summary: A proposed competitive application centered on reads, pressure, identity, and incomplete information—not wagering.
archive.provenance: Product boundary synthesized from user direction and diagnostic criticism.
archive.body:
## Product premise

Para Poker should use poker's durable competitive meanings—reads, pressure, incomplete information, identity, history, and rivalry—without importing deposits, wagering, rake, cash-equivalent chips, or paid competitive power.

## Current caution

The archived competitive circuit requires paid-only K-XP for major qualification and makes unsupported claims of legal safety. That document is a risky product-strategy artifact, not an implementation specification.

archive.title: Reath
archive.summary: Provisional project scope for the developed mortal civilizations, timelines, and associated visual archive.
archive.provenance: Provisional scope created to prevent world-specific lore from binding all EGGS games.
archive.body:
## Provisional role

Reath currently functions as the safest scope for Rumin, Frumo, Bizi, Sheen, their characters, timelines, and locations. This prevents those materials from silently becoming ecosystem-wide foundation canon.

Its relationship to Paralleon, Para, and EGGS still requires a user decision.

archive.title: Signal Reader
archive.summary: A player who interprets unstable information early and changes plans without becoming trapped by certainty.
archive.provenance: Prototype archetype translating Zendra into a constructive player promise.
archive.body:
## Player promise

You notice what a changing situation is trying to say before others do.

Signal Reader describes observable play—selective bluffing, adaptation, and information discipline. It must not label a player paranoid, manipulative, delusional, or morally suspect.

archive.title: Zendra
archive.summary: Perception, influence, signal interpretation, and the point where meaning changes possible action.
archive.provenance: Synthesized from Zendra principle prose and the Xen'Dra observer poem.
archive.body:
## Core question

What is real once enough minds obey it?

Zendra is the inner battlefield: attention, interpretation, prediction, memory, art, propaganda, empathy, belief, and mistrust.

## Constructive expression

Imagination, empathy, insight, reframing, artistic transformation, and the ability to read unstable situations.

## Failure mode

Fear becomes evidence. Symbols become commands. A population acts on ghosts because shared meaning has become heavier than observable reality.

## Mechanical vocabulary

Reveal, conceal, predict, bluff, misread, reframe, signal, and distort.

remediation.title: Define Para Poker's non-gambling product premise
remediation.problem: Para Poker is framed as part of the desired reuse model, but its boundaries are not yet a settled product statement.
remediation.why: Poker language can cause mechanics, marketing, or monetization to drift toward wagering assumptions.
remediation.affected: Foundation specification; future Para Poker documents and prototypes.
remediation.fix: Define Para Poker around reads, incomplete information, pressure, history, rivalry, and identity, with explicit exclusions for wagering, deposits, rake, and cash-equivalent chips.
remediation.output: Approved Para Poker product premise and exclusions.

remediation.title: Remove paid-only competitive legitimacy
remediation.problem: The competitive circuit requires K-XP from paid events for major qualification while claiming payment is optional.
remediation.why: This is structurally pay-to-advance and conflicts with the project's player-first philosophy.
remediation.fix: Retire or rewrite paid-only XP, tickets, weighting, placement legitimacy, and required paid pathways. If paid events remain, ensure equivalent competitive qualification paths.
remediation.output: Revised qualification philosophy and circuit model.
remediation.workType: Product strategy writing; legal/design guardrail; canon decision

remediation.title: Reconcile symbolic recognition with XP architecture
remediation.problem: The MDP rejects automated points and favors human recognition, while the circuit proposes multiple grindable XP currencies.
remediation.why: Product direction is internally inconsistent and may produce engagement farming.
remediation.fix: Decide which stages use human recognition, earned records, ratings, contribution evidence, or XP. Define what XP must never represent.

remediation.title: Define competitive prestige without spending proxies
remediation.problem: The circuit explicitly treats K-XP as a proxy for money spent and uses paid perks to create prestige.
remediation.why: This reduces identity and legitimacy to transaction history.
remediation.fix: Base prestige on verified skill, sportsmanship, contribution, seasonal performance, difficult accomplishments, and recorded rivalry history.
remediation.output: Prestige model and prohibited monetization patterns.

remediation.title: Separate product strategy from creative canon
remediation.problem: MDP and circuit proposals are stored beside cosmology and lore without layer labels.
remediation.why: Temporary operational ideas may be mistaken for evergreen creative commitments.
remediation.fix: Reclassify them as dated business/product strategy artifacts, link relevant guardrails, and create successor documents rather than altering sources.
remediation.output: Product artifact classifications and supersession links.

remediation.title: Retract unsupported legal-safety claims
remediation.problem: The competitive circuit declares ticket/XP structures legally clean without qualified analysis.
remediation.why: Labels and non-cash terminology do not by themselves determine legal treatment.
remediation.affected: `INTRODUCTION to Competetive circuit (2).pdf`, especially ticket and prize-funding sections.
remediation.fix: Mark legal claims risky, prohibit reuse as guidance, and require jurisdiction-specific counsel for paid entry, prizes, chance, wagering, or redeemable value.
remediation.output: Legal-review warning record and red-flag summary for counsel.
remediation.needsDecision: No to flag; Yes plus qualified counsel before implementation

remediation.title: Create monetization guardrails
remediation.problem: The archive lacks approved boundaries for paid events, cosmetics, progression, scarcity, and competitive advantage.
remediation.why: Product proposals can silently recreate extraction or pay-to-win dynamics.
remediation.affected: MDP; competitive circuit; Para Poker; future games.
remediation.fix: Define prohibited, review-required, and presumptively acceptable patterns, including paid-only qualification and leaderboard weighting.

remediation.title: Define prize and tournament review triggers
remediation.problem: No standard triggers review when a design adds entry fees, prizes, tickets, or cash equivalents.
remediation.why: Risk depends on mechanics, jurisdiction, participant age, prize funding, and marketing—not terminology alone.
remediation.affected: Competitive circuit; all future tournament plans.
remediation.fix: Create a mandatory intake checklist and blocking review flag for any payment/prize/chance/value combination.
remediation.needsDecision: No for drafting; qualified counsel for final legal checklist

remediation.title: Define community content rights and consent
remediation.problem: Co-creation is encouraged without submission terms, licenses, privacy rules, or withdrawal handling.
remediation.why: EGGS may not have clear rights to store, modify, publish, or commercialize contributed work.
remediation.affected: MDP community loop; future submissions and profiles.
remediation.fix: Develop plain-language contribution terms and internal review procedure with qualified counsel.
remediation.output: Contribution rights requirements and counsel-ready questions.

remediation.title: Review cultural and symbolic harm controls
remediation.problem: The ethics codex is principled but absolute in places, while current materials contradict it and use recognizable architecture/symbols.
remediation.why: An unworkable rulebook may be ignored; a vague one may not prevent harm.
remediation.affected: Ethics codex; civilization prose; concept art.
remediation.fix: Convert the ethics codex into operational checks with escalation triggers, examples, and documented exceptions rather than unsupported assurances.
remediation.output: Revised cultural/fiction design guardrail and review worksheet.
